researchQuestion: Does an input-cost shock transmit differently across route-specific Taiwan issuers, and is pass-through visible before or with realized margin/volume changes?

clocks.materialKnownAt: conservative first research capturedAt unless official release timestamp is separately frozen
clocks.issuerFundamentalClock: actual issuer report publication knownAt, not fiscal quarter end
clocks.stockOutcomeClock: first eligible Taiwan trading session after materialKnownAt; CLOSED until sample/readiness gate passes

issuerFundamentalReports: first issuer-reported quarter whose publication knownAt occurs after materialKnownAt
second issuer-reported quarter whose publication knownAt occurs after materialKnownAt

primaryRouteContrast.exposed: 2006 東和鋼鐵 / EAF / high direct scrap exposure
primaryRouteContrast.differentRouteControl: 2002 中國鋼鐵 / BF-BOF / iron ore-met coal primary route plus secondary converter scrap

requiredStateBeforeOpeningOutcomes: energy/electricity and inventory-buffer state KNOWN or explicitly UNKNOWN
no post-outcome remapping of issuer route or benchmark
noSyntheticMarginRule: Do not define company gross margin as output benchmark minus input benchmark. A benchmark spread is a process-price descriptor only unless route weights, units, yield, energy, inventory, freight and product mix are evidenced.
falsification: If high- and lower-exposure routes react similarly after market/sector controls, route-specific material edge may be redundant.
If output prices pass input cost but realized margin still falls, pricing benchmark is not sufficient evidence of pricing power.
If margin improves without benchmark pass-through, mix/volume/energy/inventory or other factors may dominate.
If results depend on changing lag windows after outcome inspection, reject as data snooping.
If only one material episode drives the effect, keep descriptive only.
